# Momentum and Exponential Moving Averages

Momentum transforms gradient descent from a memoryless method into one that accumulates velocity — damping oscillations and accelerating progress in consistent directions. EMA is the mathematical core.

## Classical Momentum: The Heavy Ball Method

mₜ = β·mₜ₋₁ + gₜ; θₜ₊₁ = θₜ − η·mₜ. Expanding: mₜ = Σₖ βᵏ·gₜ₋ₖ — exponentially weighted past gradients.

## Effective Learning Rate

In consistent gradient direction: mₜ → g/(1−β). Effective LR = η/(1−β). β=0.9 → 10× amplification. In oscillating directions: momentum cancels (damping).

## Convergence Speedup on Ill-Conditioned Problems

Quadratic with condition number κ: pure GD needs O(κ) iterations; momentum GD needs O(√κ) with optimal β* = ((√κ−1)/(√κ+1))². Quadratic speedup.

## EMA as a Low-Pass Filter

mₜ = β·mₜ₋₁ + (1−β)·gₜ is a discrete IIR filter. Attenuation of high-frequency gradient noise; pass-through of consistent directions. Effective window: 1/(1−β) steps.

```python
def ema_update(ema_params, model_params, decay=0.9999):
    for ema_p, p in zip(ema_params, model_params):
        ema_p.data.mul_(decay).add_(p.data, alpha=1 - decay)
```

## SGD Momentum vs. Adam's First Moment

SGD: vₜ = β·vₜ₋₁ + gₜ (unnormalised). Adam: m₁ₜ = β₁·m₁ₜ₋₁ + (1−β₁)·gₜ (normalised EMA) + bias correction + adaptive scaling by √m̂₂.

> **Warning:** High β (0.99+) creates stale momentum — slow recovery after LR changes or distribution shifts. Reset momentum buffer when changing training phases.
